chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mu'tamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who arrives in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah; if the Asr prayer is missed before he enters the state of Ihram for the 'Umrah, does he lose the 'Umrah? He said: 'He has [the right to perform it] for what is between him and the sunset of the sun.' And he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had done that.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj)
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: The Umrah (ritual visit) associated with Tamattu'
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, the day pilgrims proceed to Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mu'tamatti' misses the Asr prayer before entering Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the temporal validity of the Ihram for Umrah al-Tamattu', establishing that if a pilgrim arrives in Mecca on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah after Asr, the Ihram remains valid until sunset, thereby preserving the ritual's integrity. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) anchors this ruling in the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), demonstrating the continuity of prophetic practice in Hajj jurisprudence. This ruling is significant for resolving practical disputes regarding the timing of entering the state of consecration relative to the daily prayer schedule.
